title: Rings are ring objects of $\Ab$
statement:
Give $\Ab$ the monoidal structure $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ with unit $\mathbf Z$ and its usual
associator, unitors and symmetry $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$. For a ring $R$ let
$\eta_R\colon\mathbf Z\to R$, $n\mapsto n\cdot1$, and let
$\mu_R\colon R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\to R$ be the map with $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. Then:

1. $(R,\mu_R,\eta_R)$ is a ring object of $\Ab$ ([det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]);
2. every ring homomorphism $f\colon R\to R'$ is a morphism of ring objects, so $R\mapsto(R,\mu_R,\eta_R)$
   is a functor from rings to $\mathrm{Mon}(\Ab)$;
3. if $R$ is commutative, then the ring object $R$ is commutative.

proof.text: Regard the underlying additive group of any ring $R$ as a $\mathbf Z$-module by integer multiples. Distributivity gives $(a+a')b=ab+a'b$ and $a(b+b')=ab+ab'$; induction on nonnegative integers and then additive inverses give $(na)b=n(ab)=a(nb)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Thus multiplication is $\mathbf Z$-bilinear. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with base ring $\mathbf Z$, supplies the unique additive map $\mu_R:R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\to R$ satisfying $\mu_R(a\otimes b)=ab$. Also $\eta_R(n)=n\cdot1$ is additive since $(n+n')\cdot1=n\cdot1+n'\cdot1$. Every additive map of abelian groups is $\mathbf Z$-linear: it preserves positive repeated sums, zero and additive inverses.

source.place: Opening paragraph; tensor universal property is Stacks 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: By the generation assertion in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], two additive maps out of $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}N$ are equal if they agree on all $x\otimes y$: their difference vanishes on generators and hence on every finite integer linear combination. This also applies to three factors: write an element of $(M\otimes N)\otimes P$ as a sum of $u_i\otimes p_i$ with integer coefficients, expand each $u_i$ as a sum of $m_{ij}\otimes n_{ij}$ with integer coefficients, and distribute using bilinearity. The result is an integer linear combination of $(m\otimes n)\otimes p$. For additive maps $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, the tensor map $f\otimes g$ is the unique map supplied by the same universal property to the bilinear map $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)\otimes g(y)$; in particular $(f\otimes g)(x\otimes y)=f(x)\otimes g(y)$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, reduction to pure tensors; Stacks 00CX generation and bilinearity

proof.text: The associativity equation required by [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid] has source $(R\otimes R)\otimes R$. Under the usual associator stipulated in the statement, $(a\otimes b)\otimes c$ maps to $a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. Thus $\mu_R\circ(\mu_R\otimes\mathrm{id})$ takes this generator to $(ab)c$, whereas $\mu_R\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mu_R)\circ\alpha$ takes it to $a(bc)$. These are equal by the ring associativity law. Step 2, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], extends the equality from these generators to the entire source.

The left-unit equation of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid] is checked on $n\otimes b\in\mathbf Z\otimes R$: the composite $\mu_R\circ(\eta_R\otimes\mathrm{id})$ gives $(n\cdot1)b=nb$, which is exactly the stipulated usual left unitor. The equality $(n\cdot1)b=nb$ follows by distributing the repeated sum of $1$ for $n\ge0$ and then taking additive inverses for $n<0$. For the right-unit equation, on $a\otimes n\in R\otimes\mathbf Z$ the composite $\mu_R\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\eta_R)$ gives $a(n\cdot1)=n(a1)=na$ by the integer-linearity proved in step 1 and the ring right-unit law $a1=a$. In particular, for $n=-k<0$ one has $a((-k)\cdot1)=a(-(k\cdot1))=-a(k\cdot1)=-ka=na$. This is the usual right unitor. The generation statement in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extends each equality to its full source. Together with step 3 these are exactly the three monoid-object axioms, proving clause 1.

Let $f:R\to R'$ be a unital ring homomorphism. Its underlying additive map obeys $f\mu_R(a\otimes b)=f(ab)=f(a)f(b)=\mu_{R'}(f\otimes f)(a\otimes b)$. Generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] makes this an equality of maps. For every integer $n$, additivity and $f(1)=1$ give $f(\eta_R(n))=f(n\cdot1)=n\cdot1=\eta_{R'}(n)$, including negative $n$ since $f$ preserves additive inverses. These are precisely the multiplication and unit compatibility equations in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], so $f$ is a ring-object morphism.

Define the object assignment on rings by the ring-object structure constructed in steps 1, 3 and 4, and the morphism assignment by the underlying additive map in step 5. The identity ring homomorphism has the identity additive map, and the underlying additive map of $g\circ f$ is the composite of those of $f$ and $g$. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], composition and identities in $\mathrm{Mon}(\Ab)$ are these same underlying maps, and its forgetful functor is faithful. Consequently the two functor equations hold, completing clause 2.

Now suppose $R$ is commutative. The given symmetry sends $a\otimes b$ to $b\otimes a$, so $\mu_R\circ\beta_{R,R}$ sends it to $ba=ab=\mu_R(a\otimes b)$. Generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extends this equality to all of $R\otimes R$. It is the braided commutativity equation in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], proving clause 3. No commutativity of multiplication was used in clauses 1 and 2.
